questions.question_text: Evaluate $\int_{-12}^{-3} \dfrac{1}{x}\,dx$, giving the answer as a single logarithm.

options.why: Subtracted the value at the upper limit from the value at the lower limit.
Took the logarithm of the difference between the limits, $-3-(-12)=9$, then added a negative sign because the integrand is negative.
Multiplied the two limits instead of dividing them.
Added the values at the two limits instead of subtracting them.
Divided $4$ by $\dfrac{1}{2}$ instead of subtracting.
Subtracted in the wrong order, taking the upper value from the lower one.
Lost the minus sign when splitting $\dfrac{6x-1}{2x}$ into two terms.
Took the logarithm of the numerator instead of the denominator.
Integrated the numerator and the denominator separately, as if there were a quotient rule.
Forgot to divide the numerator by the coefficient of $x$.
Left out the constant of integration and never used the condition $f(0)=4$.
Treated $\ln 1$ as $1$ when substituting $x=0$ to find $C$.
Substituted the limits into $\dfrac{1}{3}\ln|3x-12|$ without checking the zero denominator at $x=4$.
Ignored the zero denominator at $x=4$ and reversed the subtraction, using $\dfrac{1}{3}(\ln 9-\ln 6)$.
Assumed the areas on opposite sides of the asymptote cancel, although the integrand is undefined at $x=4$.

questions.solution_text:
$3x-12 = 0$ when $x = 4$.
$x = 4$ lies between the limits $1$ and $6$, so $\dfrac{1}{3x-12}$ is undefined inside that interval.
$\int_{1}^{6} \dfrac{1}{3x-12}\,dx$ is undefined.

questions.question_text: Find the exact value of $a$, where $a > 0$, if $\int_{a}^{6} \dfrac{2}{x}\,dx = 2$.

options.why: Solved $\ln a = \ln 6 + 1$, reversing the sign when rearranging.
Did not divide by the factor $2$ before exponentiating, using $\ln 6 - \ln a = 2$.
Correctly divided the integral value by $2$, but also incorrectly halved the upper limit, using $\ln 3-\ln a=1$.
